title: FNOL Claims Intake Triage & Adjudication Support Agent
problem: First notice of loss (FNOL) arrives as call transcripts, web-form submissions, and scanned PDF packets (police reports, repair estimates, medical bills) with no common structure. Manual intake and adjuster routing takes 25–40 minutes per claim, and mid-size carriers report 15–20% SLA breach rates on initial contact windows during normal volume — far worse during CAT events. Missed fraud signals and misrouted claims contribute to claim leakage industry-wide estimated at 5–10% of incurred losses.
solution: A trigger-extract-validate-route agent normalises FNOL from any intake channel into a structured, confidence-scored claim record, validates it against policy coverage terms via RAG over the policy document store, runs parallel fraud-signal checks against claims databases and prior history, and routes the claim to the correct adjuster queue by complexity and risk. Every payout authorization stops at a mandatory human approval gate — the agent surfaces evidence and a recommendation, never authorizes payment itself.
whoItsFor: Claims Adjusters, Claims Intake Coordinators, SIU (Special Investigations Unit) Analysts, Claims Operations Managers
workflowSteps: Trigger: FNOL received via call-center recording, web portal submission, or scanned/emailed PDF packet

IntakeAgent normalises the source — transcript segmentation for phone claims (speaker-diarised), structured field parse for web forms, OCR + layout extraction for scanned PDFs (police reports, repair estimates, medical bills)
ExtractionAgent produces a structured claim record — policy number, loss date, peril type, location, parties, described damages, requested amount — with a per-field confidence score

PolicyValidationAgent retrieves the policy record from the policy admin system and checks coverage via RAG over indexed policy documents: policy active on loss date, peril covered, applicable limits/deductible, endorsement exclusions

FraudSignalAgent runs in parallel: claim-timing vs. policy inception check, cross-source narrative consistency check (call transcript vs. web form vs. police report), prior claim history lookup (ISO ClaimSearch), staged-loss pattern check (LexisNexis C.L.U.E.)
Orchestrator merges validation and fraud results into a triage packet with a complexity/risk score
Routing gate: low-complexity, no-flag claims route to the fast-track adjuster queue; high-value, multi-peril, or fraud-flagged claims route to a senior adjuster or SIU queue
Adjuster reviews the pre-loaded triage packet (extracted data, coverage validation, evidence-linked fraud flags), requests additional documentation if needed

HITL approval gate: any reserve or payout authorization requires explicit adjuster/supervisor sign-off — the agent never authorizes payment; on approval, writes the payment instruction to the claims/disbursement system
Audit log entry recorded for every decision with a full evidence snapshot
keyInsights: The leverage is in normalising three structurally incompatible intake formats — call transcript, web form, scanned PDF — into one confidence-scored record before any coverage or fraud logic runs; validation built on ambiguous extraction just produces confident-sounding wrong answers. Fraud checks must stay evidence-linked signals for a human to weigh rather than silent auto-declines, because an over-aggressive false-positive rate quietly defeats the entire triage system by routing everything back to manual review.

architectureNotes: Extraction runs per-channel with channel-specific confidence models — ASR word-error-rate for calls, OCR confidence for scans — so downstream validation can apply different thresholds per source type instead of treating all extracted fields as equally reliable. PolicyValidationAgent and FraudSignalAgent run in parallel and are deterministic-overlay checks (coverage rules, database lookups) rather than LLM judgment calls, keeping the auditable decision trail out of free-text generation. The routing gate is a soft triage step (queue assignment), but payout authorization is a hard, code-enforced HITL gate — the two must never be conflated, since misrouting a claim is recoverable but an unauthorized payout is not.

failureModes.mode: Fraud false-positive rate routes most claims to manual review, defeating the purpose of triage
failureModes.mitigation: Use tiered flags instead of a single binary: a soft flag stays in the fast-track queue with an annotation for the adjuster to weigh, a hard flag (multiple corroborating signals) routes to SIU. Calibrate thresholds monthly against analyst-verdict feedback and track precision/recall as a platform SLO.

failureModes.mode: OCR failure or low-confidence extraction on poor-quality scanned police reports
failureModes.mitigation: Per-field confidence threshold; fields below threshold are flagged on the triage packet and routed to a manual data-entry queue. Never auto-populate a coverage decision on an unverified loss detail — store raw scan alongside structured output for audit.

failureModes.mode: Policy administration system unavailable during coverage validation
failureModes.mitigation: Circuit breaker with fallback to a cached policy snapshot (TTL 1h) tagged with a staleness flag; claim is held in a 'pending coverage verification' state rather than blocked from intake entirely.

failureModes.mode: Adjuster queue misrouting on ambiguous or multi-peril claims (e.g., storm-driven water damage spanning property and catastrophe queues)
failureModes.mitigation: Complexity classifier returns a multi-label output rather than a single forced category; ambiguous claims default to a senior generalist queue instead of silently picking one queue, with the ambiguity itself surfaced to the adjuster.

scalingConsiderations: FNOL volume spikes 10–50x during catastrophe (CAT) events — queue-based ingestion with autoscaling extraction workers is required, not optional, for hurricane/hail/wildfire response.
Structured extraction compresses per-claim intake from 25–40 minutes (manual) to under 4 minutes regardless of source channel mix.
Fast-track auto-routing rate should target 50–65% of standard first-party claims; monitor monthly — a sudden spike may indicate fraud-threshold drift rather than genuinely cleaner claims.
Claims database APIs (ISO ClaimSearch, LexisNexis) typically bill per lookup and rate-limit; cache repeat entity (policyholder, VIN, address) lookups within a rolling 30-day window.
State-level claims-handling deadlines vary (e.g., prompt-pay statutes); SLA timers must be state-aware, not a single global clock.
